name: led
summary: An indicator LED and its series resistor, driven from a logic output
note: The resistor is the smallest stocked value that holds the LED to current_a at its lowest forward voltage (and so below its own maximum current). The LED's anode goes to the resistor, its cathode to ground, so the output drives it high. A green (InGaN) LED needs up to 3.1 V: from a 3.3 V output it may barely light, so red is the default.

current_a.note: The most current the output should source

led.note: KENTO 0603 LEDs. Their drawings mark pin 1 as the anode; on KiCad's footprint pad 1 is the cathode, so the part is placed by its cathode mark, not by its pin numbers

requires.message: a {led} LED needs up to its maximum forward voltage plus headroom; from this drive it may not light (use red, or drive it from a higher rail)

citations.note: Min and max; no typical. DC forward current 25 mA (p.3). Polarity only in the drawing, p.2: pin 1 '+'.
Min and max. DC forward current 30 mA (p.3).
